_comment: Every value the Dashboard shows, and the thing that OWNS it. CLAUDE.md
rule 7: the Dashboard gathers, it does not work things out. If a fact is
first computed on that page, that is the bug, and it presents as two
screens telling reception different things about the same villa.
The nav_canon.json pattern. This table is what the page must read; the
suite asserts the page actually calls each reader, and that the patterns
under `banned` appear nowhere in it. Whichever side a change misses
Adding a value to the Dashboard means adding a row here first. If you
cannot name an owner, you are about to originate a fact on a page whose

reads.value: pre-arrival form state, and the arrival-sheet chips that mirror it
reads.note: Front Desk's three states. Never recompute from `at` or the answers.

reads.value: a guest's dinner answer when no /dinner cell was ever written
reads.note: Arrival night only, cell wins the moment anyone sets one. Reading /dinner alone showed villa 4 grey here while Invitations had it answered, 8 Sep.

reads.value: stays, dinner cells and each villa's pre-arrival, for the day
reads.note: One reader, so this board and the two it summarises cannot disagree.

reads.value: today's booked treatments and where each one's morning text stands
reads.note: Spa reminders' own gatherer (28 Sep): the treatments booked on the day, each judged by spaReminderState, both in nala-shared.js and held to tests/spareminder_cases.json. The card and the sending page read the same rows, so they cannot disagree about who is owed a text. It replaced this page's own walk of /spa through dayOf.

reads.value: the room number on a spa chip
reads.note: A spa record keys by BOOKING id and carries no villa; the viewed night's stay row carries that id, so the villa is the row holding it - spaReminderRows makes the join from the rows fetchStays read. A join of two owned facts, not a new one.

reads.value: which cards each arriving villa holds
reads.note: The card table counted, never worked out: a villa is carded when it holds rows (the model, 11 Sep). Held to tests/cardstate_cases.json with cardState. The card is a door to Keys, which owns issuing and the register; an Encode button here would be this page originating an action it cannot watch.

reads.value: how many lost cards float, across every date
reads.note: The one judge of a row, held to tests/cardstate_cases.json. A lost card is an attention fact until its expiry retires it, so the note carries it whatever the day's cutting looks like.

reads.value: whether a guest has physically arrived
reads.note: Front Desk stamps checkedInAt. Deliberately duplicated one line on this page; see the comment there.

reads.value: tonight's menu
reads.note: Returns the LIVE node without a date guard - only its menu.json fallback checks. The date and filled-courses guards are menuCheck's, in tally.html.

reads.value: diners with no villa, both shapes
reads.note: Digital replies under /responses with no room, and staff-added ext- keys under /manual. Reading /manual alone lost every externally booked table that came in through a link.

reads.value: how many people a dining row is
reads.note: One head unless the record says otherwise. Counting a pax-less dining row as nought undercounts the kitchen.

reads.value: where a villa stands on tonight's invitation
reads.note: Invitations' own reader. kind 'ready' is still to ask, and a FAILED send is 'ready' - the reconstruction this replaced counted it as sent.

reads.value: which villas are still owed a dinner invitation
reads.note: Keyed by VILLA, written and read by invitations.html. /previnvites is the pre-arrival SMS log, keyed by booking id, and is a different thing entirely.

reads.value: which villas are still owed a PRE-ARRIVAL SMS, over the 14-day window
reads.note: arrivals-sms.html's own reader, shared so the send page and this board cannot disagree about who is to send. 'ready' is unsent, sendable and not yet engaged; sent, opened and completed drop off. Held to tests/presms_cases.json, read by both suites.

reads.value: a booking's pre-arrival SMS send record
reads.note: Keyed by BOOKING id, written by the Worker and read by arrivals-sms.html. Read whole and plucked by id now (one read, not a fetch per booking - the HTTP/1.1 fan-out fix), the same node however it is read. /invites is the dinner invitation, keyed by villa - a different thing entirely, one node over.

reads.value: which spa treatments have been texted, and what each text quoted
reads.note: Keyed by BOOKING id then treatment id, written by the Worker and read by spa-reminders.html, read whole here. Not on the /spa record, which spa.html writes whole and would wipe.

reads.value: whether a still-to-send booking's last SMS attempt FAILED (the red pill), pre-arrival and spa reminder alike
reads.note: The finer reading over the send record, shared so the Dashboard's red-ring pill agrees with the red words on the sending page's row. A failure is red (colour law); a never-asked one is grey. Held to tests/presms_cases.json. The spa reminder log is written by the same Worker in the same shape, so the spa card's red ring reads it too.

reads.value: a booking's arrival date
reads.note: Builds a LOCAL date from an ISO day, and handles the dd/mm/yyyy the PMS also writes.

reads.value: whether a timestamp falls on the day being viewed
reads.note: With dkey. A stamp is UTC and a day is local: 9:58am on the 8th in Australia is 2026-09-07T23:58Z.

reads.value: a staff member's name against a print tick
reads.note: The tick stores the staff key, so a rename follows it. shortTagFor is the upper-case chip form and shouts inside a sentence.

reads.value: which cards a role may open
reads.note: The app's own keys: resSheet and cleansBoard, not the resBoard/cleanBoard you would guess.

owns.why: The app cannot see paper, so nothing else can know this. The only fact this page originates.

banned.why: Slicing an ISO stamp compares a UTC date against a local day. It read a published menu as not published on 8 Sep, and would have done so every morning before 10am.
